Package br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.infrastructure.stream

Class FfmpegRecorder

java.lang.Object
br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.infrastructure.stream.FfmpegRecorder
public final class FfmpegRecorder extends Object
The FFmpeg process that records the phone's stream into a ring of one-second segment files, for as long as the application runs.

The ring is larger than any buffer reads from it: the spare segments are what keep FFmpeg from overwriting a second while a clip is still copying it.

This is the only process that reads the phone. Some phone apps (DroidCam) serve their video to a single client, so anything else that wants the live picture — the spectator broadcast — reads the relay this process publishes on the loopback instead of asking the phone a second time.

    • READ_TIMEOUT_MICROSECONDS

      public static final long READ_TIMEOUT_MICROSECONDS
      How long FFmpeg waits on a stream that sends nothing before it gives up and exits. A phone that leaves the Wi-Fi closes no connection, so without this the read would block forever and nobody would learn the phone is gone.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

  • Constructor Details

    • FfmpegRecorder

      public FfmpegRecorder(String streamUrl, Path bufferFolder, int relayPort)
      Prepares a recorder of the phone at streamUrl; nothing runs until start().
      Parameters:
      streamUrl - the phone's stream address, such as http://192.168.0.42:8080/video
      bufferFolder - the folder the ring of segments is written to
      relayPort - the loopback UDP port the recorded video is also published on
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the address is not an http, https or rtsp address with a host, the folder is missing, or the port is not a valid one

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start() throws IOException
      Empties the buffer folder and starts recording into it. Segments left from an earlier run belong to a moment nobody is watching any more.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the recorder is already running
      IOException - if the folder cannot be cleared or FFmpeg cannot be started

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Asks FFmpeg to finish cleanly, and kills it if it does not. Safe to call more than once, and on a recorder that never started.

    • onExit

      public void onExit(Runnable action)
      Runs the action if FFmpeg exits without being asked to — typically the phone dropping off the network. An exit stop() asked for is not reported. The action runs on a background thread.
      Parameters:
      action - what to do when the recording ends on its own
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the recorder was never started

    • segmentList

      public Path segmentList()
      The file FFmpeg appends each finished segment to; SegmentLog reads it.
      Returns:
      the segment list inside the buffer folder, which may not exist yet

    • liveRelay

      public String liveRelay()
      The address another FFmpeg reads to receive the video this recorder encodes, as it is encoded. Nobody listening costs nothing: the datagrams are simply dropped. A reader gives up after READ_TIMEOUT_MICROSECONDS without a packet, which is how a dropped phone reaches it too.
      Returns:
      the loopback UDP address of the relay
